I was really looking forward to this game, I loved BB1. But adding a limit to the number of times you can use skills has just killed the game for me. There are some really neat changes in this game but having to micromanage skill uses is something I am not interested in worrying about.

Skills have a limited number of uses for each floor of the dungeon. This stupid system led to even stupider deaths like dying on the 3rd floor boss fight because my only attack skill ran out of uses. Why didn't I pick up a second attack skill? Because the few skill drops I did get were all either buffs or heals. This turns fun runs into frustrating experiences that end when they shouldn't have. I will keep trying the game to see if this actually stops murdering runs after I've built up good lab parts and such. Though, nothing as frustrating like dying from having zero offensive skill uses left when you're about to kill a boss. EDIT: Yes, it does keep happening. Some monsters are designed around screwing over your skill usage counts so you auto-die. This skill usage ♥♥♥♥ needs to go ASAP! General Overview: The majority of the issues I had with the first game being confusing seems to have been dealt with. The map for dungeon access is crystal clear with where things are. Clicking races/classes you don't have unlocked has a window popup tell you where you can unlock them while still letting you see what their stats/abilities are. Dungeons actually tell you what their floor limit is instead of going forever. There's a Buriedpedia that shows you the monster's base stats and effects. Unfamiliar effects can be clicked to see what they do. I like the game but the skill usage limit just feels bad.

I was really looking forward to this, but I simply can't recommend it. Lots of new battle changes have borderline ruined, or at the very least far too heavily changed, the battle flow, making it much slower and less enjoyable (eg the multiple health bars, the absolutely obscene amount of menus and piss-poor explanations for the billions and billions of concepts, generally less interesting loot, limits on the number of times which you can use a skill). I think there's potential for a real gem of a game, and I truly and sincerely want to love this game. I played the first one a lot, and while I was nowhere near as skilled or knowledgeable as other players, I felt like I had learned. Here, I'm feeling the opposite. The bombardment of mechanics that, to me, fail to complement one another, combined with the burrowing of necessary information under far too many menus and text, lead this to be very, very hard to get into. Also no fierce god :c

I played first Buriedbornes. For about 30 minutes, before I quit. This one I played a bit more, because genuinely I felt it was a bit better. So now, why negative review? After hours of playing with different builds, I just feel most mechanics are not fun. - While there is a richness of skills, abilities and the initial combinations were fun, once you unlock some OP mechanics (like executor with preemptive shots and shurikens), you wouldn't want to get back ever. - The game is pure RNG fest, which can screw even your most prepared runs. - You'll be spending hours rerolling stuff using the soulstones, to roll something of use. - Each new character and class unlocks new skills and abilities, making hard to find stuff literally almost impossible. - The grind is real; The dungeon runs, especially if you start doing 14F or 16F dungeons is not '10 minutes', it drags and drags again. - The premium currency used to unlock meta progression (in the form of unions) is awarded in such a miniscule amounts that you need to redo previous content with new combinations. You literally need 25 dungeon runs to pay for one of the advanced unions (it costs 500; you get 10 per first clear with specific race/class per dungeon). - The UI is downright poor, the mechanics are not well explained - I found out that critical ignore resistances, in most painful of ways - it's not written anywhere. On top of that there is a lot of errors in english translation (like Darkness giving +100% haste... when it's giving +100% critical, and so on) - Before I find out that there is actually a battle log, I didn't even know what killed me 99% of times. After I find it, I still doesn't know what killed me sometimes?! - There is plently of UI space, but to check Battle log you need to click right button and select battle log in the options. You cannot do that while there are skills being used. It bring it up as a separate page, and you need to close it before you can resume the fight. All that, while there is a lot of space on either right or left side to fit it, and should be able to be open/hidden by clicking on button no matter what the status of combat is. - Even mod board a.ka. talent tree is random, so you can have godlike picks for your combination, or downright crap in a specific run. - Enemies having multiple hp bars (that stop at 0 hp, allowing them to have a turn) is just tedious mechanic. It prevents racking damage and usefulness of stuff like preemptive strikes unless you cheese your way around other mechanics, like executor's crits. - Oh boy the energy drain and petrify are cool. Losing your run because not only you lose your skills by using, but enemies can instantly delete 5-8 usages by using a single ability. Which in conjuction of already mentioned multiple HP bars makes you immedietly hate locations where there are succubus and gorgons. - The successful cleaning of enemies within floors are awarded by 'Savage Mode' when reaching 150% savage counter, which makes all enemies spawn as elite/rare ones (with multiple hp bars to booth). Very. Fun. To sum it up, it's pure RNG, it's tedious, it's grindfest. There are interesting mechanics here, and a large build variety, and it's free so you can try, but the game lost it's fun factor somewhere in the creep of features, rngs and grindy content. I feel like the idea is 'Let make Dark Souls but turn based', but Dark Souls doesn't have RNG that can screw you over and over.

I played Buriedbornes 1 a lot so I'll leave a fair review for this one. [h3]First: The problems with the game series itself[/h3] - Everything is obtuse, from the beginning enemies use confusing effects and you have confusing effects that aren't explained. Usually turn-based games would start by giving you simple abilities and ramping up the complexity gradually, yet in this series it's complicated start to finish. - Goal of making a character is to burst through a dungeon. Unlike in traditional turn-based games where you are patiently taking turn after turn strategically in Buriedbornes most meta builds are untouchable and kill everything in one hit. This is kind of a necessity as you need to complete between 7 and 25 floors of a dungeon and there's about 15 enemies per floor, so if you want to complete a dungeon before you die of old age you must have a good damage output, and most enemies indeed fall in a single hit, even without meta-gaming. I see people complain about enemies having a lot of health bars and having to chip away at them. I understand the frustration; some enemies have a lot of HP but have no actual way of seriously harming you. There's also situations where you rush through a dungeon with ease and then randomly get one-shot by an enemy, this has been the case since BB1. Some enemies like Bladetooth have first-strike abilities that damage you when combat starts, so it's completely unavoidable and if the enemy has an unfortunate random buff your run is over(Unless you spend Goldshards, more on that later). - Balance sucks. I decided to look at some of the top player and most of them play a variation of executioner, either as an elf, wererabbit or halfling, since that's the most meta spec right now. There's also void damage that confuses me to no end. Why is physical and magical damage not enough? It just seems tacked on at the end of development since it's rarely mentioned in attributes, unlike physical and magical damage. [h3]Now on which issues are unique to BB2:[/h3] - Equipment, bags, contracts. In Buriedbornes1 you could just take extra skills and equipment without any restrictions. The ingame currency to purchase them was also really easy to get by just setting up a character that farms them automatically. In BB2 you first need to purchase bags to take more than one item with you at a time, then you need to spend silver coins or grind for equipment to take with you. Worst of all are contracts, which summon an end-game instance of sorts. Entering those dungeons was free in BB1, now you need to grind through union quests to get them. If you take items with you into a dungeon you lose them upon death, which would be fine if you couldn't just revive with Goldshards(€€€€) and keep going, thus paying yourself out of a penalty. This is probably where the dev makes the most money(besides skins), since you'll be paying for backpacks, then lose them in a dungeon(since obtaining the bags from union quests is a truly ungodly grind). - Localisation is even worse than BB1 and there's a lot of formatting bugs. - UI is awful, on PC it's just in portrait mode instead of using the whole screen. - There's little content to do end-game besides jail and battlefields, neither of which I find fun. Jail is a game-mode where you need to capture monsters and graft them together to create one amalgamation to use as a character, but to get these monsters you need to go into a dungeon and use a capture skill on a monster. This is where I'm not ashamed to admit that this game filtered me, since it got too complicated at that point. - Grind sucks. You now get one lab part per run instead of multiple ones like in BB1, but lab parts are now almost guaranteed to be upgrades, and function a bit differently in general. This is good if you have one main race/job combo, but if you want to play something else you're out of luck, you'll need to play on that combination to get fitting lab parts. Luckily there's no actual pressure for good lab parts, and I finished every dungeon(besides battlefield, the PvP mode) without grinding for lab parts and playing the game my way. - Rerolling sucks, you need to reroll 200 times if you're unlucky and sometimes I felt like I was playing cookie clicker. [h3]Positives:[/h3] - Nice visuals and a cool art style(said art style carries this game hard) - The customisation IS pretty neat and it's funny playing around with different combinations or race and job - I like the new "talent trees" you get when you camp - Concept of unions is nice, but you can just leave and rejoin them willy nilly and I think the dev could've made this system more concrete and less temporary - More, interesting and very dark events that are surprisingly immersive despite the terrible translation. They suck you in, especially the one in Forest. [h3]FYI[/h3] I played mostly Ghost/Halfling - Necromancer in earlygame, Ghost - Death Knight in midgame and cleared end-game content with Automaton - Taoist. I'm not entirely sure if there is such a thing as "end-game" as the difficulty seemed pretty flat to me. I used these terms in order of what you unlock when.

Upon my son's recommendation, I initially hesitated to dive into Buriedbornes 2 due to its unique art style. However, after giving it a chance, I've grown quite fond of it. I began my journey with the game on my Samsung S24 Ultra, but found the text somewhat challenging to read. Fortunately, discovering that it's available on Steam has transformed my experience for the better. I've accumulated about 10 hours of gameplay split between my phone and Steam. While the game is commendably free and developed by a small team, it does come with a learning curve. Some mechanics are not explicitly explained, or perhaps the explanations are tucked away in places I haven't yet explored. This aspect can make mastering the game a tad more challenging than usual. Despite this, the depth and enjoyment I've found in Buriedbornes 2 make it more than worthy of a positive review. It's clear that the developers have put a lot of heart into this project, and for anyone willing to navigate its initial complexities, there's a rewarding adventure waiting. I hope this version captures your thoughts more eloquently while highlighting the game's merits and areas for potential improvement. Some pros and cons... Pros: Atmosphere and Visuals: The game is often praised for its dark fantasy aesthetic which many reviewers find captivating. The artwork for characters and environments according to others usually noted for being genuinely beautiful. I think based off my experience you will either love it or hate it. I love it now though. Gameplay Mechanics: It's appreciated for its turn-based combat and roguelite elements which provide a deep and strategic gameplay experience. The non-real-time operation allows for thoughtful decision-making. I am still learning and enjoying learning something new every few hours. Replayability: It appears the game offers a high level of replayability with different character builds, dungeons, and meta-progression elements, so far I have been using a Necro, but initially I was playing a Ranger. I think the ranger was ok, but I could never get past the end bosses until I started playing the necromancer. Accessibility and Freedom: Despite its complexity, the game is designed to be accessible, with players able to choose from various skills and items, offering a personalized adventure. Again, I'm still learning and only recently realized that the crafting list changes between combat (i'm not sure what drives it yet) but sometimes i'm able to craft a Dark Knight for instance, and other times a whole different list of things are there. Cons: Learning Curve: There's a steep learning curve due to mechanics not being fully explained or being somewhat obtuse, which can be frustrating for new players. Translation and UI Issues: Some reviewers mention poor translations and a user interface that can feel cluttered or unintuitive, particularly in its mobile version. Skill Limitations: The limitation on skill uses has been a divisive feature, with some players finding it adds strategic depth while others see it as a hindrance to gameplay flow. Content and Longevity: After completing the main dungeons, there's a noted lack of content, which might affect long-term player engagement unless supplemented by future updates. 玩一代玩了好久才看见有续作。总体来说，没有一代好玩，回去玩一代了，。 一代的技能可以升级，相同的随到就升一级，这是我一个爽点，结果二代我傻了，是替换。 技能有次数也还可以吧，符文槽算是个好玩的，但是多数随到的槽都很沮丧，加这个槽还是不如升级来的爽，而且我技能都那么强了，装备那么强了，还是打不过，还几乎是次次都打不过，我麻了，，我是真不会玩。 界面为啥我点全屏，关了设置界面就会恢复成小屏，而且我自己点的放大窗口，它有些操作也会变成小的。这个界面要给我整崩溃。 UI确实精细很多了，升技能点太复杂了，随机的这个玩意我真的要疯了。 怪诞猎奇的风格还是很赞，有种什么感觉呢，好的功能扔了，加了一堆美化的，确实好看好玩了，可老的爽点别删别改。
古早的纯粹的回合制战斗玩法，简单易上头。局内技能、2代新增强化技能都丰富了游戏战斗体验。UI比较简陋但是可以接受，基本信息都有。简体中文翻译不全但是能接受，略微有点不太满意的是替换技能的时候不能预览当前技能的效果，希望能优化。

[quote][b][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtransaction]Warning: Microtransaction infested mobile app![/url][/b] This game is infested with a toxic mobile app style cash shop. You will be prompted to and expected to give money to the developers through this cash shop to buy in-game goods so you can play the game.[/quote] "Buriedbornes2 - Dungeon RPG" is one of thousands of nasty mobile apps infesting the "free" section of Steam, but it's not really free. This mobile app is NOT FREE, the developer seeks to mislead gamers by publishing it in the free section... the mobile app is timegated and you have to pay a lot of money through the cash shop to play it. That's cancer. There's only a superficial game here. The game visuals and the game itself are incredibly shallow... think of them as the too-bright, colourful, thin plastic cabinet dress theme on a poker machine at the casino. That's basically what this is. So really, the mobile app "game" is just a veneer, a thin skin wrapped around a nasty, predatory mobile app cash shop. Putting that toxic mobile app monetisation aside... this is a mobile app. I didn't spend thousands on a gaming PC so I could pretend it's an iPhone, and I don't think you did either... this kind of mobile app has no place in your Steam library. The graphics are lacklustre because this was designed for mobile phones, not gaming PCs. Whenever a product is designed to run tolerably on 5 year old iPhones, it's obviously not going to come close to the minimum quality standards that PC gaming enthusiasts expect on their cutting edge gaming rigs. Mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone. PC gamers don't spend thousands on their gaming rigs so they can pretend they're iPhones. That alone is enough to disqualify this for recommendation. Next is pricing and what value this has for gamers. This "free" game won't count toward your game collection count on your profile. With that in mind, is it something you should still download? Definitely not. This isn't worth it. I'm paraphrasing another reviewer here, but this should be a paid product... they'd have to pay people to download it.
